args.prompt:
Make a new KFB soft claymation ink blob game sprite sheet, The Language Wing. Exactly six independent complete standing ink-splat monsters, 3 columns by 2 rows, landscape 1536×1024 true transparent PNG. The two reference PNGs define the rounded dark charcoal-plum ink body and modeled white sclera, red iris, black pupil and filled dark eyelids. Silhouette is essential: face directly in one continuous whole blob, with no human neck or chest. Keep the lowest third of EVERY figure an entirely visible bare dark ink base with 3 to 5 prominent uneven rounded puddle waves or short footlike lobes growing directly from it. The base is wider than the face, thick and irregular, with a soft sculpted edge. No separate legs or shoes, flat cut ends, busts, long sleeves or full jackets. Any collar, badge or narrow sash occupies a tiny area high on the ink body. Hold props at the side or upper belly and keep the whole lower blob edge unobstructed. Tiny ink hands. Smooth softly satin plasticine, broad material folds, sparse larger handmade marks. No backdrop, shadow, floor, frame or lettering except the minimal type shapes specified in language props. Generous transparent gutters and outer margins. Six distinctive expressions and shapes. Rust, cream and marine teal, small scarf tabs and collar pins.
Row-major roles:
1. Female-read German teacher. wide scalloped blob, stern downward concentration. Key cue: three chunky sentence tiles fitted like a tiny bridge.
2. Male-read English teacher. tall bent teardrop, hopeful side-eye. Key cue: two small clay speech tokens with pictograms of a bee and a capital B.
3. Female-read French teacher. upright reverse comma, lifted eyebrow and pursed lips. Key cue: small slate with a single sculpted è and a chalk nub.
4. Male-read Spanish teacher. broad lopsided pear, delighted open smile. Key cue: small tilde-shaped clay piece held just above a miniature lowercase n block.
5. Male-read Latin teacher. low rounded trapezoid, weary half lids, tight smile. Key cue: miniature wax tablet with a short rounded stylus.
6. Male-read German as a second language teacher. narrow wavy splat, encouraging tilted gaze. Key cue: little key and two large picture cards with a door and an apple.
Render all six from the front in full with broad visible bare sculpted splat bases, each with a different wave rhythm. Keep the entire prop inside its cell.
